name: Syrma SGS Technology Ltd
tagline: EMS player executing a genuine margin turnaround - EBITDA margin from ~6% to 9-11%+ via a deliberate mix-shift out of low-margin consumer into auto/healthcare/industrial and rising ODM - but a ~Rs 28,000 Cr market cap, ~10-12% ROE and thin 4-5% PAT margins put a 10x out of reach
business_overview: Syrma SGS is a diversified Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) company serving automotive, healthcare, industrial, IT & railway and consumer segments, with a growing original-design-manufacturing (ODM) mix and an export book (medtech, plus 'Make in India' laptop assembly for MSI and Dynabook). It is investing up to ~Rs 1,595 Cr in Andhra Pradesh for advanced PCB fabrication (single/multilayer/HDI/flex) and raised ~Rs 1,000 Cr via QIP for inorganic growth.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 4,819 Cr, +27% YoY (multi-year growth ~34%/yr); some quarters revenue fell YoY as low-margin consumer was shed
FY26 guided >Rs 500 Cr (55-57% growth) vs Rs 324 Cr FY25; margin ~8% -> revised 9% -> tracking higher; Q3 FY26 EBITDA +101% YoY, exports +66%
D/E ~0.36 (reduced); 52-week range ~Rs 635 - 1,543; stock roughly doubled in 6 months
fundamentals_narrative: The investable story is a real, management-driven margin turnaround: operating EBITDA margin has moved from ~5.9% (Q3 FY24) to 9-11.6% (FY26) by deliberately slowing the high-volume, tight-margin consumer segment and growing higher-margin automotive, industrial, healthcare and IT/railway work plus ODM (16% of revenue). Q3 FY26 EBITDA was +101% YoY on +66% export growth, and FY26 EBITDA is guided at >Rs 500 Cr (55-57% growth) against a targeted 30%. A 5-year PCB anti-dumping duty is a tailwind for domestic PCB assembly. The constraint is scale and return profile: at ~Rs 28,400 Cr the company already carries a large-cap valuation, ROE is ~10-12% and PAT margin ~4-5% (structural for EMS), and reported revenue has actually declined YoY in several quarters as consumer volume was dropped.
technical_read: Not independently pulled; stock roughly doubled over six months into mid-2026 then pulled back ~7% to the 50-day EMA - forum technicians frame the ~Rs 1,187 level (200-day area) as the long-term line for holders.
sentiment_summary: 57-post thread, consistently well-informed. DeepVal, dpk1994, joinjp2003 and meekinvestor (all elevated tier) have tracked the story closely and positively across FY24-26 - the recurring theme is 'cheapest of the listed EMS leaders (Dixon/Kaynes/Syrma), and the margin overhang is lifting'. Key milestones logged in-thread: MSI and Dynabook laptop-assembly wins, the Andhra Rs 1,595 Cr PCB-fab plan, the Rs 1,000 Cr QIP, PCB anti-dumping duty, and successive quarters of sharp EBITDA/PAT growth on mix change. The main bear point (firefueled) is that management kept the headline EBITDA-margin guide at ~7-8% for a while and that revenue growth optically slowed - though later concalls raised the EBITDA guide materially.
community_signal: Multiple elevated-tier users (DeepVal, dpk1994) track Syrma positively and disclose being invested, consistently framing it as the cheapest EMS leader with an improving margin trajectory - a supportive community read, though tempered by all being self-described 'invested and biased' and none making a formal high-conviction call.

trusted_signals.note: Posted Q3 FY26 highlights: EBITDA +101% YoY (Rs 79 Cr -> Rs 159 Cr), PBT/PAT +108%, exports +66% (Rs 202 Cr -> Rs 335 Cr), ODM revenue ~16% (up from 12%), gross margin 27.4% vs 26%, and management raising FY26 EBITDA guidance to >Rs 500 Cr (55-57% growth vs a 30% target). Factual positive coverage from an elevated-tier user; elevated not core, no conviction floor active.

bse_notes: No SEBI or fraud action found. ~Rs 1,000 Cr QIP completed (for inorganic growth). Andhra Pradesh allotted 26.7 acres at Naidupeta for a PCB fab/R&D facility; total AP investment plan up to ~Rs 1,595 Cr. 5-year PCB anti-dumping duty imposed (sector tailwind). No promoter pledge issues noted.
bull_case: Genuine, management-driven margin turnaround: EBITDA margin ~6% -> 9-11%+ via deliberate mix-shift into auto/healthcare/industrial and ODM (now 16% of revenue)
FY26 EBITDA guided >Rs 500 Cr (55-57% growth) vs a 30% target; Q3 FY26 EBITDA +101% YoY, exports +66%
Structural India-EMS tailwind (PLI/ECMS/ISM 2.0), 5-year PCB anti-dumping duty, and forward integration into PCB fabrication (Rs 1,595 Cr Andhra plan)
Cheapest valuation among listed EMS leaders (vs Dixon, Kaynes); laptop-assembly wins (MSI, Dynabook) add a new vertical
Debt reduced (D/E ~0.36) and a Rs 1,000 Cr QIP war-chest for inorganic growth
bear_case: ~Rs 28,400 Cr market cap already - a 10x needs ~Rs 2.8 lakh crore, larger than Dixon today; the easy re-rating is done (stock doubled in 6 months)
Structural EMS economics: ROE ~10-12%, ROIC ~6.5%, PAT margin ~4-5% - margin turnaround helps but does not change the model
Reported revenue has fallen YoY in several quarters as consumer volume was shed - growth is now mix-quality, not volume
Capital-absorbing: large PCB-fab capex and inventory/working-capital intensity typical of EMS at scale
Execution risk on PCB fabrication - a chemically complex, capital-heavy business Syrma is entering fresh
thesis_fit: neither - a real quality-improvement story, but at a ~Rs 28,400 Cr valuation with ~10-12% ROE and thin EMS margins there is no credible path to a 10x in 2-3 years or a 100x in 10 years
verdict_headline: A genuine EMS margin turnaround, correctly recognised by the market (stock already doubled) - quality is improving, but size and structural returns keep it outside the 10x screen. thesis_fit neither, conviction Medium
verdict_reasoning: First-time coverage. The recent trend is genuinely strong - a deliberate, executing margin turnaround (EBITDA margin ~6% -> 9-11%+, FY26 EBITDA guided +55-57%) with ODM and exports growing.

But the screen fails on size and return profile: ~Rs 28,400 Cr market cap, ~10-12% ROE, ~4-5% PAT margin - the margin improvement is real but does not turn an EMS contractor into a 10x candidate, and the stock has already doubled recognising it.
Elevated-tier users (DeepVal, dpk1994, Krishna_Kumar) track it positively and one trusted_signal is logged; elevated not core, so conviction is set on fundamentals at Medium, no floor.
No red-flag tier. thesis_fit neither on size/returns; conviction Medium reflecting real execution. Not flagged for 30-day revisit (thesis_fit neither).

four_box.note: India-EMS PLI/ECMS/ISM 2.0 + 5yr PCB anti-dumping duty is a real structural tailwind; explicit size math (~Rs28,400cr, would need ~Rs2.8 lakh crore, larger than Dixon today) rules out tam; management-driven margin turnaround (EBITDA margin 6%->9-11%+) is real execution but EMS economics remain structurally thin (ROE~10-12%) — moat weak; cheapest valuation among listed EMS leaders (vs Dixon, Kaynes) — valuation yes.

track_record.note: FY21-FY26 screener. Despite ~30-60% revenue growth most years, both revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% cleared in only FY22 (+43%, ROCE 15%) and FY25 (+20%, 17%). FY23 (ROCE 10%), FY24 (12%) and FY26 (~13-15%, ROE 14%) missed on returns - EMS economics are structurally thin (ROE 10-14%), so the margin turnaround has not yet lifted ROCE durably above 15%.

quality_metrics.note: FY26 ROE 14%, ROCE ~13-15% (FY25 17%; screener FY26 not shown). Near net-cash after the ~Rs 1,000 Cr QIP (gross borrowings Rs 400 Cr vs EBITDA ~Rs 530 Cr). OPM expanded 6%->11% FY24->FY26 on a deliberate mix-shift out of consumer into auto/healthcare/industrial + ODM. But EMS is very working-capital-intensive (inventory + receivables) so cash conversion is deeply negative during the growth phase, and the fresh Rs 1,595 Cr PCB-fab entry is capital-heavy and unproven - capex_efficiency neutral.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~84x trailing needs ~40%+ EPS CAGR sustained against a ~30-35x EMS-leader exit; the EBITDA-margin step-up from ~6% to 9-11% is driving PAT faster than revenue, but ROE is still ~10-14% and the stock has already doubled in six months
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: revenue ~Rs 6,000-6,500 Cr (+25-35%), EBITDA margin ~10-11%, PAT +40-60% on operating leverage + mix
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: revenue ~Rs 7,500-8,500 Cr, PAT growth moderating as the margin re-rating matures and PCB-fab capex weighs
market_expectation.gap_basis: 84x trailing P/E on a ~4-5% PAT-margin, ~10-14% ROE EMS contractor; the fast EBITDA-margin step-up (6%->9-11%) is a one-time mix re-rating, not a repeatable driver. Our FY28 PAT is well below the 40%+ CAGR the multiple embeds, and the stock has already doubled pricing the turnaround.
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view
